hints: Look at the two separate effects of lowering temperature, it changes both how fast equilibrium is reached and where the equilibrium position lies.
The forward reaction is exothermic with $\Delta H^\ominus = -9.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so think about which direction is favoured by cooling using Le Chatelier's principle.
Combine a slower fall from the same 0.5 start with a final flat line for $\text{I}_2$ that must sit below 0.23 to find the matching shape.
walkthrough:
**Check the starting point**

All graphs must start at the same place. You begin with equal amounts of $\text{H}_2(g)$ and $\text{I}_2(g)$ and no $\text{HI}(g)$, so the mole fraction of $\text{I}_2$ is 0.5 at time = 0.

Chemical system:
$$\text{H}_2(g) + \text{I}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI}(g)$$

**Effect of lower temperature on rate**

Lower temperature means particles have less kinetic energy and fewer successful collisions per second. So the curve falls more gently and takes longer to flatten out.

Rule to remember: lower $T$ = slower rate = shallower gradient.

**Effect of lower temperature on equilibrium position**

The forward reaction is exothermic. Cooling favours the exothermic direction to release heat, so equilibrium shifts to the right.

This means more $\text{I}_2$ is used up, so the equilibrium mole fraction of $\text{I}_2(g)$ must be lower than 0.23.

**Pick the matching graph**

You need a curve starting at 0.5, falling more slowly than the original, and levelling off below 0.23. That is exactly the shape that shows both the kinetic and equilibrium effects of cooling.

options.A: This shows a slower reaction but the same final mole fraction of 0.23. It correctly shows the rate effect but forgets that temperature also shifts the position of equilibrium for this exothermic reaction.
options.B: This is correct. It starts at 0.5, falls more slowly because the lower temperature slows the rate, and levels off below 0.23 because cooling shifts the exothermic equilibrium to the right, using up more I2.
options.C: This reaches the same 0.23 value even faster than the original. Lower temperature cannot speed up the reaction, and it cannot leave the equilibrium position unchanged when $\Delta H$ is not zero.
options.D: This levels off above 0.23, meaning more I2 remains. That would mean a shift to the left on cooling, which is backwards. Cooling favours the exothermic forward reaction, not the endothermic reverse.
